content: Penicillin V Potassium is an antibiotic prescribed to treat specific bacterial infections, including pneumonia, scarlet fever, and infections of the ear, skin, and throat. It is also used to prevent recurrent rheumatic fever and chorea. Antibiotics like Penicillin V Potassium are ineffective against colds, flu, or other viral infections. This medication may sometimes be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Penicillin V Potassium is available in tablet and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken every six hours (four times a day) or every eight hours (three times a day). Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take Penicillin V Potassium exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Shake the liquid form well before each use to ensure the medication is evenly mixed. Swallow the tablets whole with a full glass of water. Continue taking Penicillin V Potassium even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Before taking Penicillin V Potassium, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, tartrazine (a yellow dye found in some processed foods and drugs), or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, especially other antibiotics, anticoagulants (blood thinners) like warfarin (Coumadin), atenolol (Tenormin), aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) like naproxen (Anaprox) or ibuprofen (Motrin), oral contraceptives, probenecid (Benemid), and vitamins. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney or liver disease, allergies, asthma, blood disorders, colitis, stomach problems, or hay fever. Let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking Penicillin V Potassium, contact your doctor immediately. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking this medication. Take Penicillin V Potassium at least one hour before or two hours after meals. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Penicillin V Potassium may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: upset stomach, diarrhea, vomiting, or mild skin rash. If you experience severe side effects, such as a severe skin rash, itching, hives, difficulty breathing or swallowing, wheezing, or a vaginal infection, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep the tablets at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Discard any outdated or unused medication. Store the liquid form in the refrigerator, tightly closed, and discard any unused liquid after 14 days. Do not freeze the liquid. The liquid form is stable for seven days at room temperature. Consult your pharmacist about proper disposal of unused medication. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your response to Penicillin V Potassium. If you have diabetes, use Clinistix or TesTape (not Clinitest) to test your urine for sugar while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If you still have symptoms of infection after completing the prescribed course, contact your doctor.
